chapter.title: Scope
chapter.para: This specification defines an MCP-based interface for ONVIF devices, enabling AI agents to discover and use device capabilities without relying on SOAP. MCP is natively supported by agentic clients and provides a standard way to expose device functions and metadata.
The objective is to broaden the range of clients that can interoperate with ONVIF devices and to expose advanced, ready-to-consume device functions for AI agents.

section.title: Background
section.para: Traditional physical-security systems are built around devices that expose predefined services, events, metadata, and configuration interfaces. ONVIF clients, including video management systems, use these interfaces to configure devices and ingest information into a site-centric operational view.

AI-enabled and agentic systems introduce additional consumers and interaction patterns. These systems need to discover available capabilities, retrieve contextual information, interpret semantically described data, and invoke permitted actions across devices, analytics services, and other site systems.

The ONVIF Agentic Service connects these environments. It complements existing ONVIF services by providing common information models and discovery mechanisms that can be used by both traditional clients and AI-native applications. Initial use cases include a VMS ingesting standardised site-centric metadata and an authorised AI application using MCP to discover and access device configuration capabilities.

section.title: Motivation
section.para: Without standardisation, AI integrations depend on vendor-specific data models, capability descriptions, and agent tools. This increases integration cost and limits portability across manufacturers and system components.

This specification defines the interoperable boundary between information producers and consumers. It enables consistent exchange of semantic metadata, provenance, confidence, spatial and temporal context, and capability descriptions, while reusing existing ONVIF services and security mechanisms where applicable.

The objective is not to prescribe a complete agentic architecture or replace established VMS workflows. The objective is to allow traditional physical-security systems and AI-native systems to share trusted information and expose controlled functionality through standardised contracts.

chapter.title: Overview
chapter.para: Agentic configurations are handled through the Agentic Service. Agentic configurations are used to configure and control the intelligent functions as defined in this specification. YAML for this service is specified in http://www.onvif.org/yaml/agentic.yaml.

section.title: MCP — The Agentic Tool Interface
section.para: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open, JSON-RPC 2.0 based protocol designed to connect AI language models and agents to external tools and data sources. In the ONVIF agentic stack, MCP serves as the standardised interface layer between the ONVIF Client (acting as an MCP Host) and each ONVIF Device (acting as an MCP Server). Adopting MCP means that any ONVIF Client can invoke any compliant ONVIF Device without requiring a vendor-specific driver.

section.title: Protocol Primitives
section.para: MCP defines three categories of server-side object that a host may discover and use:

listitem.para: Tools are callable operations with a named identifier, a human-readable description, and an inputSchema (JSON Schema) that fully describes the expected arguments. In the ONVIF agentic stack, Tools are called Skills and represent ONVIF Device capabilities such as configuring a detection region or querying service status. The ONVIF Client invokes a Skill by sending a tools/call JSON-RPC request over the Control Plane.

Resources are read-only data objects accessible via resources/list and resources/read requests. In this specification, Resources carry the LinkML schema bundles that describe the event payloads and skill input parameters of the ONVIF Device. Each schema resource carries the MIME type application/linkml+yaml.
Prompts are optional server-defined interaction templates. This specification does not mandate Prompt support; ONVIF Devices MAY expose Prompts for human-in-the-loop workflows.

section.title: Transport Modes
section.para: This specification normatively uses the Streamable HTTP transport. The ONVIF Client sends JSON-RPC requests as HTTP POST to the ONVIF Device's /mcp endpoint, and the ONVIF Device returns each response on the same request/response exchange, as defined by the Streamable HTTP transport in MCP 2026-07-28. This specification does not use a separate, long-lived, server-initiated streaming channel: metadata events are retrieved by the ONVIF Client via the request/response events/poll operation, or delivered out-of-band via the events/subscribe webhook mechanism (see ). An ONVIF Device conforming to this specification shall support the Streamable HTTP transport and shall support events/poll; support for events/subscribe webhook delivery is OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED for deployments where the ONVIF Client is not able to poll at the cadence required by the use case.

section.title: Protocol Version
section.para: This specification normatively requires MCP 2026-07-28. Implementations conforming to this specification shall not use the session-era MCP 2025-11-25 protocol.

MCP 2026-07-28 is a fully stateless protocol. There is no session establishment handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id header. Every HTTP request is self-contained: the ONVIF Client includes the MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28 request header on each call, together with the Authorization: Bearer JWT header. The ONVIF Device shall reject requests that carry a protocol version other than 2026-07-28 with HTTP 400.

Service discovery uses the server/discover JSON-RPC method, which replaces the initialize / initialized handshake of earlier versions. The response carries the server's capability flags (tools, resources, prompts) and its human-readable identity. As required by MCP 2026-07-28, the ONVIF Device shall implement server/discover. The ONVIF Client may call server/discover before issuing other requests to learn supported versions and capabilities, but it is not required to call it first and may invoke any operation directly and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.

The stateless model is the correct choice for the ONVIF Agentic Service use case: ONVIF Devices are deployed as horizontally-scalable endpoints behind load balancers, and pinning a ONVIF Client to a specific server instance via a session identifier would prevent transparent failover and scaling. With MCP 2026-07-28, every request can be routed to any instance of the ONVIF Device without loss of state.

section.title: LinkML — Schema Definition Language
section.para: LinkML (Linked data Modeling Language) is an open schema definition language that describes data structures in YAML. In the ONVIF agentic stack, LinkML is the normative language for defining both the structure of metadata events (delivered via events/poll or webhook) and the argument shapes of Skills invoked via tools/call. LinkML defines the schema; JSON-LD (see ) is the runtime wire format that carries instances of that schema.

section.title: Schema Structure
section.para: A LinkML schema document is a YAML file with the following top-level keys:

listitem.para: id: a globally unique URI that serves as the schema identifier. This URI is reused as the JSON-LD @context value in every event payload emitted by the ONVIF Device, making the schema self-locating.

imports: a list of schema URIs from which common types are inherited. ONVIF maintains a shared type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines reusable structures such as bounding boxes, polygon regions, timestamps, and confidence scores. ONVIF Devices SHOULD import this library rather than redefining common types.

classes: named data structures with typed attributes, optional range constraints (minimum_value, maximum_value), and documentation strings. The root event class shall extend BaseAnalyticsEvent from the ONVIF common type library.
enums: closed value sets used for categorical fields such as SeverityLevel (low, medium, high, critical) and event type discriminators.

section.title: Dual Role: Event Schema and Skill Input Schema
section.para: The same LinkML model serves two distinct purposes within the stack:

listitem.para: For metadata events, the compiled JSON Schema derived from the LinkML model is used by the ONVIF Client LinkML Validator to check every incoming metadata event for structural correctness — required fields, numeric ranges, and valid enum values.

For Skill invocation, the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool (Skill) definition is also derived from the same LinkML model. This guarantees that the coordinate spaces, unit definitions, and vocabulary used to configure the ONVIF Device (e.g., a detection region polygon) are identical to those used to report events, eliminating a class of integration errors that arise when configuration and reporting use incompatible data models.

section.title: Compilation to JSON Schema
section.para: The LinkML toolchain provides a generator that produces a JSON Schema document from a LinkML YAML source. This compiled JSON Schema is used in two places:

listitem.para: First, it is embedded in the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool definition returned by tools/list. The ONVIF Client can validate skill arguments against this schema before sending a tools/call request, providing early client-side error detection.

Second, a copy of the compiled schema is stored in the ONVIF Client Schema Registry after schema discovery. The registry uses the compiled schema to validate every incoming metadata event, whether retrieved via events/poll or delivered via webhook, before the ONVIF Client processes it.

section.para: ONVIF Devices shall pre-compile their LinkML schemas at build time and include the compiled JSON Schema in Tool definitions. The source YAML shall also be exposed as a schema Resource so that the ONVIF Client can re-compile or audit the schema independently.

section.title: ONVIF Common Type Library
section.para: The ONVIF AI Working Group maintains a shared LinkML type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines base classes and enumerations used across all ONVIF Devices. Key types include:

BaseAnalyticsEvent: the mandatory root class for all metadata events, defining the required fields event_id (UUID), timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), source_uri, confidence (float, 0.0–1.0), and severity (SeverityLevel enum).
BoundingBox and PolygonRegion: normalised coordinate structures shared between event payloads and skill input schemas to ensure consistent spatial referencing.

ONVIF shall not redefine any type declared in the common type library. This ensures that an ONVIF Client that has already loaded the common library does not need to re-fetch it for each new ONVIF Device it connects to.

section.title: JSON-LD — Wire Format for Metadata Events
section.para: JSON-LD (JSON-based Linked Data) is the serialisation format used for all metadata events delivered via events/poll or webhook. Where LinkML defines the schema at design time, JSON-LD carries instances of that schema at runtime. The two technologies are complementary: LinkML declares what data looks like; JSON-LD is the payload that conforms to that declaration.

section.title: Context and Type Annotations
section.para: Every metadata event emitted by an ONVIF Device shall include two mandatory JSON-LD keywords:

@context: a URI that points to the canonical LinkML schema for this event type. The value shall equal the id field of the LinkML schema from which the event class is derived. This URI is the primary key used by the ONVIF Client Schema Registry to look up the compiled JSON Schema for validation.

@type: the class name of the event as declared in the LinkML schema (e.g., FireDetectionEvent, PersonCrossingEvent). This field allows the ONVIF Client to route the event to the appropriate handler without inspecting the full payload.

Together, @context and @type make each event self-describing: an ONVIF Client that receives an event with an unfamiliar @context URI knows exactly where to fetch the schema needed to understand and validate the event.

section.title: Self-Describing Events and Dynamic Schema Registration
section.para: 1. Suspend validation of the triggering event.
2. Fetch the LinkML schema YAML from the URI identified by @context, or issue an MCP resources/read request to the originating ONVIF Device to retrieve the latest schema bundle.
3. Register the schema bundle in the local registry.
4. Re-validate and process the suspended event against the newly registered schema.

This mechanism allows an ONVIF Device to introduce a new event type (e.g., a firmware update that adds a VehicleTypeDetectionEvent) without requiring a pre-coordinated ONVIF Client update. The ONVIF Client self-heals its schema knowledge at runtime.

section.title: Relationship to Linked Data
section.para: Although full JSON-LD processing (graph expansion, context dereferencing, SPARQL querying) is not required by this specification, the use of JSON-LD framing ensures forward compatibility with semantic web tooling. A conformant ONVIF Client shall treat @context and @type as opaque identifiers for schema lookup and event routing. An ONVIF Client MAY additionally perform full JSON-LD processing for downstream applications such as knowledge graph ingestion or cross-vendor event correlation.

section.title: Architecture Overview
section.para: The ONVIF agentic Protocol Stack is structured around the standard ONVIF roles of an ONVIF Client and an ONVIF Device, with an OIDC Authorization Server acting as the shared trust anchor that issues the tokens consumed by both. The figure below shows the top-level relationships between these three components and the single MCP channel that carries all interactions between them.

figure.title: ONVIF agentic Protocol Stack — Top-Level Architecture

section.para: The OIDC Authorization Server is the trust anchor for the entire stack. It issues signed ES256 JWTs to the ONVIF Client via the OAuth2 Client Credentials grant, and exposes a JWKS endpoint that the ONVIF Device uses to validate every token it receives.

The ONVIF Client combines the ONVIF Client role with the MCP Host role. It manages connections to ONVIF Devices, invokes skills, and retrieves metadata events. It also maintains the LinkML Schema Registry and validates every incoming event before it is passed to business logic.

The ONVIF Device provides an MCP Server endpoint. Through this endpoint, it exposes skills in the form of MCP Tools, makes JSON-LD metadata events available as MCP Events, and, when webhook delivery is supported, posts those events to a client-supplied HTTPS callback. Moreover, it announces the LinkML schema via MCP Resources.

All communication between the ONVIF Client and the ONVIF Device is bearer-token authenticated and carried over a single MCP channel: every operation defined by this specification — capability discovery, skill invocation, resource retrieval, and event delivery — is a JSON-RPC request/response exchange over MCP 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP to the ONVIF Device's /mcp endpoint. There is no separate, server-initiated streaming channel. When webhook delivery is used, the resulting event POSTs travel outside this MCP channel, directly from the ONVIF Device to the HTTPS callback endpoint supplied by the ONVIF Client (see ).

section.title: Protocol Stack
section.para: The ONVIF agentic protocol stack uses a single MCP channel, protected by TLS and bearer tokens issued by the OIDC Authorization Server, over which the ONVIF Client sends all JSON-RPC requests to the ONVIF Device.

entry.para: ONVIF Client to ONVIF Device (request/response); ONVIF Device to a client-supplied HTTPS callback endpoint for webhook event delivery.
Discover capabilities, list and invoke skills, retrieve resources, and retrieve or subscribe to metadata events.
HTTP POST to /mcp over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, events/list, events/poll, events/subscribe, and events/unsubscribe.
TLS 1.3 with an Authorization: Bearer ES256 JWT on every request.

section.para: Each request is self-contained and shall be validated independently by the ONVIF Device before execution. A response shall report either the requested result or an MCP error indicating why the operation could not be completed. events/poll, events/subscribe, and events/unsubscribe follow this same request/response pattern; their detailed behavior, including the out-of-band webhook delivery mechanism, is defined in .

section.title: Identity and Authorization Server
section.para: The ONVIF Agentic Service requires an OAuth 2.1 Authorization Server, as specified in the ONVIF Security Service Specification.

This server acts as the trust anchor for the complete stack: it authenticates clients, issues bearer access tokens, and exposes the metadata and key material needed by ONVIF Devices to validate tokens before processing MCP requests.

In practice, the Authorization Server provides centralized identity and access control for every operation. It ensures that only authorized ONVIF Clients can invoke Skills via tools/call and retrieve or receive protected metadata events via events/poll or webhook delivery, according to the roles and claims contained in the issued token.

section.title: Network Discovery
section.para: MCP 2026-07-28 does not define network-level device discovery. Therefore, ONVIF Device discovery remains dependent on the mechanisms specified by [ONVIF Core]. An ONVIF Client shall discover ONVIF Devices and obtain their service endpoint using the ONVIF Core discovery procedures before initiating MCP requests.

section.title: Service Discovery
section.para: An ONVIF Device that supports the Agentic Service shall advertise the MCP service endpoint URL through the ONVIF Core service discovery mechanism. In the ONVIF Core GetServices response, the corresponding Agentic Service entry (tds:GetServiceResponse) shall contain the service address used by the ONVIF Client for MCP requests.

section.title: Session Initialization
section.para: An ONVIF Device implementing the Agentic Service shall implement the server/discover JSON-RPC method as required by MCP 2026-07-28. The ONVIF Client MAY call server/discover as its first request on a new connection to obtain the device's protocol version, server identity, and capability flags. Alternatively, the ONVIF Client MAY call any other operation directly and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (JSON-RPC error code -32022) if the protocol version is not supported. In that case the ONVIF Device shall include a supported list in the error response and the ONVIF Client shall retry using one of the listed versions.

The server/discover response shall contain: protocolVersions — the list of MCP protocol versions supported by the device; identity — the server name and version; capabilities — the declared capability flags (tools, resources, prompts, and supported extensions). The ONVIF Client shall use the returned capabilities flags to determine which subsequent operations are available before invoking them.

The ONVIF Client is not required to keep a channel open to receive metadata events: it retrieves them on demand via events/poll, or subscribes for webhook delivery via events/subscribe, as defined in . See for wire format examples.

section.title: Schema Retrieval
section.para: The ONVIF Agentic Service exposes its LinkML metadata schema as one or more MCP Resources. An ONVIF Client shall retrieve the schema bundle before processing any metadata event delivered via events/poll or webhook.

The schema retrieval procedure is:
The ONVIF Client calls resources/list. The response includes one or more resources with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml identifying the schema files.
The ONVIF Client calls resources/read for each schema resource URI returned in step 1, in the order listed. A schema bundle may span multiple resources when imported type definitions are split across files.
The ONVIF Client registers the complete schema bundle in its validator.

An ONVIF Device shall advertise at least one resource with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml describing the structure of every event type it emits. The schema shall be self-contained — it shall not require the ONVIF Client to resolve external URIs to validate event payloads.
See and for wire format examples.

section.title: Capability Discovery
section.para: Capability discovery shall be performed through the MCP resources/read operation using the reserved URI capabilities://www.onvif.org/ver10/agentic.

An ONVIF Device implementing the Agentic Service shall expose capabilities://www.onvif.org/ver10/agentic and shall return the Agentic Service capabilities document when that URI is requested via resources/read. The capabilities document describes the features supported by the device, such as supported functions, event classes, and optional extensions. It shall also declare the events capability ({"events": {"listChanged": true}}, per the MCP Events extension) together with, for each declared event type, the delivery modes supported ("poll", "webhook", or both — see ).
Exposing capabilities for other ONVIF services is optional. When provided, the same URI pattern shall be used, replacing ai with the service name: capabilities://onvif/<service-name>.
See and for wire format examples.

section.title: Tool Discovery
section.para: The ONVIF Device exposes its Skills — callable operations — as MCP Tools. The ONVIF Client discovers the available Skills by calling tools/list.

Each Tool entry in the tools/list response shall contain:
name — the Skill identifier used in subsequent tools/call requests.
description — a human-readable description of the Skill's function.
inputSchema — a JSON Schema object that fully describes the expected arguments. This JSON Schema is compiled from the LinkML model retrieved in and shall use the same coordinate spaces, unit definitions, and vocabulary as the event payloads delivered via events/poll or webhook delivery.

The ONVIF Client shall validate Skill arguments against the inputSchema before sending a tools/call request. After completing tool discovery the ONVIF Client has obtained, without any out-of-band documentation: the complete catalogue of Skills supported by this device instance; the argument types, valid ranges, and required/optional fields for each Skill; and human-readable descriptions suitable for display or automated orchestration.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: Skill Invocation
section.para: ONVIF Agentic Skills are invoked via the MCP tools/call JSON-RPC method. The ONVIF Device shall validate the arguments object against the inputSchema of the named Skill before executing it. If validation fails, the ONVIF Device shall return a structured error response without executing the Skill.

The ONVIF Device shall advertise support for the MCP Tasks extension in server/discover. Before returning a task result, it shall verify that the client declared io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks support for the request. A supported Skill invocation may return either its normal result or a result with resultType: "task". The returned task shall include a durable taskId, a status, a ttlMs, and a recommended pollIntervalMs. The client shall use tasks/get until the task reaches completed, failed, or cancelled.

This specification defines five mandatory Skills that every ONVIF agentic device shall implement regardless of device type (camera, NVR, access control, or other). Additional device-type-specific Skills may be defined in ONVIF profiles or vendor extensions.

section.title: get_status
section.para: The get_status Skill returns the current operational status of the agentic analytics engine. It takes no arguments. The ONVIF Device shall always respond successfully to this Skill unless the device is unreachable.

The response structuredContent shall include:
state — one of running, stopped, degraded, or error.
activeFunctions — list of active function executions. Each execution shall include the function identifier and its executionId.
engineVersion — version string of the agentic engine firmware.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: list_functions
section.para: The list_functions Skill returns the set of functions supported by this device instance, together with their current configured/available state. It takes no arguments. This is the authoritative machine-readable catalogue of what this device can do; the ONVIF Client shall call list_functions before calling configure_function, execute_function, or stop_function.

Each entry in the response structuredContent.functions array shall include:
name — function identifier drawn from the ONVIF function vocabulary (for example fire_detection, face_recognition, license_plate_recognition, tailgating_detection).
enabled — boolean indicating whether this function is configured and available for execution.
configSchema — URI of the LinkML class in the schema bundle (retrieved in ) that defines the structure of the config argument accepted by configure_function for this function.
An ONVIF Device that exposes no local functions shall return an empty functions array.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: configure_function
section.para: The configure_function Skill applies a configuration to a named function. It is a generic wrapper: the structure of the config argument is defined by the LinkML schema class identified by the configSchema URI returned by list_functions for that function. The ONVIF Client shall validate config against the compiled JSON Schema (the inputSchema of the Skill) before sending the request.

The configure_function Skill arguments are:
function (string, required) — the function identifier, as returned by list_functions.
config (object, required) — the configuration object whose structure is specific to function and defined by the corresponding LinkML schema class.

configure_function shall not start the function. On success the ONVIF Device shall confirm the applied configuration. If the operation is long-running and the client has declared support for the MCP Tasks extension, the device may return a task result instead of the final result. The client shall use tasks/get until the task reaches a terminal state. On failure it shall return a structured error identifying the failing field and the violated constraint.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: execute_function
section.para: The execute_function Skill starts an execution of a configured function. It shall not be used to provide the function's configuration. The arguments shall include the function identifier and may include execution-specific parameters.

On successful start, the device shall return an executionId. If starting the function is asynchronous and the client has declared support for MCP Tasks, the device may return a task result. The task represents only the start operation and shall reach a terminal state when the execution is running or has failed. It shall not remain permanently in working while a continuous function is active.

For continuous functions, subsequent output shall be made available as metadata events, retrievable via events/poll or delivered via webhook (see ). The execution remains active until stopped or it terminates independently.

section.title: stop_function
section.para: The stop_function Skill stops an active function execution identified by its executionId. If stopping the execution is asynchronous and the client has declared support for MCP Tasks, the device may return a task result. The task represents only the stop operation and shall reach a terminal state when the execution is stopped or the stop operation has failed.

section.title: Event Delivery
section.para: Metadata events are exposed by the ONVIF Device as MCP event types, discovered via events/list and retrieved or delivered through one or both of the two delivery modes defined by this specification: poll (events/poll) and webhook (events/subscribe / events/unsubscribe), as defined by the MCP Events extension (see ). This specification does not define, and an ONVIF Device conforming to it shall not require, a long-lived server-initiated streaming channel for event delivery.

section.title: Event Type Catalogue
section.para:
An ONVIF Device shall advertise its event types via events/list. Each entry shall include:
name — the event type identifier, matching the @type value used in delivered payloads (for example FireDetectionEvent).
delivery — the non-empty subset of "poll" and "webhook" supported for this event type. An ONVIF Device shall support "poll" for every event type it declares; "webhook" support is OPTIONAL.
inputSchema — a JSON Schema describing valid subscription arguments (for example a sensor or zone filter).
payloadSchema — a JSON Schema describing the shape of the event data field. For this specification, payloadSchema is the JSON Schema compiled from the LinkML class identified by the event's @context/@type pair (see ).

If the set of event types, or the descriptor of any of them, changes at runtime, the ONVIF Device shall send notifications/events/list_changed and the ONVIF Client shall re-call events/list to refresh its registry.

section.title: Poll-Based Delivery
section.para: An ONVIF Device shall support events/poll for every declared event type. The ONVIF Client calls events/poll with the event name, subscription arguments, and a cursor (null on the first call). The ONVIF Device returns {events[], cursor, truncated, hasMore, nextPollMs}. Each entry in events[] is an EventOccurrence carrying eventId, name, timestamp, and data (the JSON-LD event payload).

The ONVIF Client shall persist the returned cursor and pass it back on the next call so that delivery resumes from that position. The ONVIF Device MAY bound replay using the client-supplied maxAgeMs, and shall set truncated: true whenever events were skipped because the supplied cursor fell outside the retention window. When hasMore is true, the ONVIF Client shall poll again immediately, ignoring nextPollMs, to drain the backlog. The ONVIF Client shall apply a configurable floor (default 1000 ms) to nextPollMs to guard against a misbehaving device inducing a tight polling loop.

section.title: Webhook-Based Delivery
section.para: Where declared for an event type, an ONVIF Device MAY additionally support webhook delivery. The ONVIF Client registers an https callback URL and a whsec_-prefixed signing secret by calling events/subscribe with name, subscription arguments, delivery: {"mode": "webhook", "url", "secret"}, a starting cursor, and a suggested lifetime ttlMs. The ONVIF Device returns a server-derived subscription id, the granted expiry refreshBefore, and a safe-to-persist cursor.

The ONVIF Device shall then POST each matching EventOccurrence to the registered callback URL, signed per Standard Webhooks (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature headers) and carrying X-MCP-Subscription-Id. Unless the ONVIF Client requested, and the ONVIF Device granted, no expiry (ttlMs: null / refreshBefore: null), the ONVIF Client shall re-call events/subscribe with the same subscription key before refreshBefore elapses to keep the subscription alive. The ONVIF Client calls events/unsubscribe to explicitly terminate a webhook subscription; otherwise it lapses at TTL expiry.
events/subscribe and events/unsubscribe shall only be accepted from an authenticated principal; an ONVIF Device shall reject unauthenticated calls to either method with -32012 Forbidden (see ).

section.title: Error Codes
section.para: An ONVIF Device shall report error conditions on events/poll, events/subscribe, and events/unsubscribe using the following JSON-RPC error codes, as defined by the MCP Events extension:

entry.para: The request is statically invalid — subscription arguments do not match the event type's inputSchema, the callback delivery.url is malformed or non-https, or delivery.secret is not a valid whsec_ value.
An unknown event name, or no subscription matching the key on events/unsubscribe.
The authenticated principal is not permitted for this event/arguments combination, or its access was revoked, or the call was unauthenticated.
A device-imposed limit or quota was reached (for example, the maximum number of concurrent subscriptions).
The request is well-formed but a requested delivery mode is not offered for this event type.
A client-supplied callback endpoint failed verification or could not be reached (webhook mode only).

section.para: See for a complete wire format example.

section.title: Dynamic Schema Re-registration
section.para:
The @context URI in each event is a live pointer to the schema that defines it. If the ONVIF Client receives an EventOccurrence whose @context URI is not already registered in its schema bundle, it shall:
Suspend validation of that event without discarding it.
Call resources/read with the @context URI to fetch the LinkML schema YAML from the ONVIF Device.
Register the retrieved schema in its validator.
Resume validation of the suspended event and all subsequent events of that type.

This mechanism allows the ONVIF Device to introduce new event types — for example after a firmware update — without requiring the ONVIF Client to have prior knowledge of the new schema. The ONVIF Device shall ensure that the @context URI is always resolvable via resources/read for as long as the device emits events of that type.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: Post-Handshake ONVIF Client Knowledge
section.para: An ONVIF Agentic Service is self-describing: an ONVIF Client that has completed the sequence defined in , , , , , and is fully operational without any out-of-band documentation, SDK, or static configuration. The table below summarises the knowledge accumulated at each step.

entry.para: Device identity, supported protocol versions, declared capability flags (resources, tools).
Complete LinkML schema bundle; JSON Schema for event validation and skill argument validation.
Device feature set, supported functions, events capability and per-event-type delivery modes.
Skill catalogue: name, human-readable description, and inputSchema for each skill.
Which functions are currently enabled; configSchema URI per function.
Event type catalogue; live metadata events retrieved via poll or delivered via webhook; @type for routing; @context for dynamic schema re-registration.

section.para: An ONVIF Device implementing this specification shall ensure that an ONVIF Client completing the above sequence is able to: validate all incoming event payloads against the registered schema; invoke any available Skill with correctly structured arguments; and interpret the full feature set of the device — all without consulting any resource external to the ONVIF Device.

chapter.title: Authentication and Authorization
chapter.para: The ONVIF Agentic Services delegates all authentication and token management to the mechanisms defined in the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. Those documents govern JWT token format and required claims (iss, aud, exp, nbf, roles), the mandatory ES256 signing algorithm, token validation rules, the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow, authorization server configuration, and TLS transport requirements. Implementations shall comply with the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. This chapter defines only the ONVIF AI-specific normative mapping of MCP operations to ONVIF access classes.

section.title: Role-to-MCP Operation Mapping
section.para: The ONVIF Security Service Specification defines three predefined JWT role values carried in the roles claim of every access token: onvif:User, onvif:Operator, and onvif:Administrator. These correspond to the ONVIF user levels and cover the majority of deployments. For environments that require finer-grained access control, the Security Service Specification defines a full user role management model that allows custom roles to be assigned to individual users; refer to the ONVIF Security Service Specification for details. The onvif: namespace prefix is reserved; custom roles shall not use it.

Anonymous access to any MCP endpoint is not permitted. Every request to the ONVIF Device shall carry a valid Authorization: Bearer JWT. The ONVIF Device maps the access class required by each MCP operation against the roles claim in the presented token and rejects requests that do not satisfy the minimum role requirement with HTTP 403. A token carrying onvif:Administrator satisfies all lower access class requirements; a token carrying onvif:Operator satisfies READ_SYSTEM in addition to ACTUATE.
The table below is normative. Each Skill exposed via tools/list shall include an annotation declaring its access class. The ONVIF Device shall enforce this mapping at runtime.

chapter.title: Metadata
chapter.para: This chapter defines the data model for structured metadata produced and consumed by ONVIF AI-enabled devices. All metadata payloads are instances of, or derived from, the abstract classes defined here. The normative schema is expressed in LinkML; JSON-LD is the wire format (see ).
The following figure shows the class hierarchy structure from which specialised metadata classes are derived. The remainder of this chapter defines and details the classes shown in the figure.

section.title: InformationItem
section.para: InformationItem is the abstract base container for any single unit of information exchanged in the metadata model. It is intentionally generic so that different semantic categories can reuse the same trust and context fields. In this specification, InformationItem is specialised by Observation and Assertion.

Each InformationItem carries the following fields: a confidence value expressing the confidence level of the contained information; a generation timestamp; a provenance field describing the origin or producer of the information; and an optional signature field that can be used to guarantee integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation of the content. The signature field is optional because equivalent protection can be provided at envelope level, as specified in .

section.title: InformationEnvelope
section.para: InformationEnvelope is an optional container used to group one or more InformationItem instances and apply a single signature to the grouped content. This enables a producer to protect multiple information elements with one cryptographic operation instead of signing each item independently.

The envelope-level signature is optional and is intended for deployments where cryptographic acceleration resources on the device are constrained. In such environments, signing one envelope can reduce signing workload while still providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation coverage for all enclosed InformationItem instances.

section.title: Observation
section.para: Observation is a concrete InformationItem representing a measurement generated internally by an ONVIF Device. It captures directly observed or computed device outputs as information items that can be consumed by downstream systems.

section.title: Assertion
section.para: Assertion is a statement supported by one or more InformationItem elements. Therefore, a statement can be supported directly by Observation instances, by other Assertion instances, or by a combination of both.

section.title: Assertion sanity checks
section.para: To achieve robust and reliable parsers, the following sanity checks are required for assertions:

listitem.para: Supporting InformationItem elements shall be resolvable, i.e., they shall have been received previously.
The assertion timestamp shall be more recent than the timestamps of all supporting elements.
The resulting dependency graph shall be directed and acyclic.
By traversing the directed acyclic graph, each assertion shall be traceable back to one or more initial observations.

section.title: Signature
section.para: Signature is an abstract class nested within InformationItem that describes a cryptographic attestation bound to the item content. Different deployments can require different signature formats and trust frameworks; for this reason, the class is abstract and shall be specialised by concrete signature profiles.

The presence of a Signature object at item level is optional. When omitted, integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation claims can still be provided by an enclosing InformationEnvelope as defined in .

section.title: JsonLDSignature
section.para: JsonLDSignature is the first concrete subclass of Signature. It attests the integrity of an InformationItem by means of a JSON-LD Data Integrity proof , as defined in W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0. The ECC signature algorithm and key parameters shall conform to the ONVIF Security Baseline.

section.title: Signing procedure
section.para: The ONVIF Device shall compute the proof using the Add Proof algorithm defined in W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 with W3C RDF Dataset Canonicalization 1.0 (RDFC-1.0) as the canonicalization algorithm. The digest and signing algorithms shall be those mandated by the current version of the ONVIF Security Baseline.

section.title: Proof fields
section.para: JsonLDSignature carries the following fields, aligned with the DataIntegrityProof structure defined in W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0:

listitem.para: type (mandatory) — fixed string "DataIntegrityProof".

cryptosuite (mandatory) — identifies the cryptosuite used. The value shall correspond to the algorithm profile mandated by the current version of the ONVIF Security Baseline. It is included in the proof configuration and therefore covered by the signature.
created (mandatory) — ISO 8601 UTC datetime at which the proof was created.
verificationMethod (mandatory) — URI of the public key or verification method that can be used to verify the proof.
proofPurpose (mandatory) — fixed string "assertionMethod".
proofValue (mandatory) — the encoded digital signature over hashData as defined in the signing procedure above.

section.title: Location
section.para: Location is an abstract class nested within InformationItem that represents the spatial origin of the information item. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: Timing
section.para: Timing is an abstract class nested within InformationItem that provides an authoritative time reference for the information item, independent of the device system clock. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: Vendor Extensions
section.para: ONVIF follows the convention, established in its WSDL-based specifications, of providing a generic extension point in every data structure to allow implementers to carry vendor-specific information without breaking interoperability. This specification carries that convention into the LinkML metadata model through the Extensible mixin.

The Extensible mixin adds a single optional, repeatable slot named extension to any class that includes it. Each entry in the slot is an instance of VendorExtension, which pairs a mandatory vendor namespace URI with a locally named, arbitrarily typed value. The namespace URI uniquely identifies the vendor and prevents naming collisions between different implementers.

An ONVIF Client that encounters an extension entry whose vendor_namespace it does not recognise shall ignore that entry and shall not treat its presence as an error. An ONVIF Device shall not use the extension slot to carry information that is required for correct interpretation of the normative fields of the enclosing class.

The Extensible mixin is applied to Observation, making the extension point available on every concrete observation class derived from it. Other abstract classes in this chapter (Signature, Location, Timing) may also include the mixin in future revisions as needed.

appendix.title: Example Call Sequence (informative)
appendix.para: This annex is informative and provides an example end-to-end sequence with sample values.

section.title: Network discovery (ONVIF Core)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends ONVIF Core discovery requests (for example WS-Discovery Probe) to locate devices on the network.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns discovery responses (for example ProbeMatches) with the Device Service endpoint.

section.title: Service discovery (ONVIF Core GetServices)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls ONVIF Core GetServices on the Device Service endpoint.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns GetServiceResponse including the Agentic Service entry with MCP endpoint URL (example: https://192.0.2.10/mcp).

section.title: Session initialization
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls server/discover to obtain the device identity, supported protocol versions, and capability flags.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns its identity, the list of supported protocol versions, and its capability flags.

Legacy client rejection (informative): A legacy client connecting with a pre-2026-07-28 protocol version (for example via an initialize request) will receive an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. The ONVIF Device shall not support protocol versions prior to 2026-07-28 and shall always include the supported list so that the client can retry.

Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends the server/discover request to https://192.0.2.10/mcp as its first request on the connection, as defined by MCP 2026-07-28. No additional channel is opened; the session initialization exchange is a single JSON-RPC request/response, and the ONVIF Client retrieves metadata events later via events/poll or events/subscribe, as shown in .

section.title: Agentic capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://www.onvif.org/ver10/agentic.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the Agentic Service capabilities document.

section.title: Optional non-agentic capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://onvif/<service-name> (example: capabilities://onvif/media).
Response (Device to Client — not supported): If the requested service capability is not exposed, the ONVIF Device returns a resource-not-found error.

section.title: Schema resource inventory
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/list to enumerate all resources, including LinkML schema resources.

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns available resources. Resources with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml are the schema files to be retrieved in (example URIs: linkml://www.onvif.org/ver10/agentic/events).

section.title: Schema retrieval
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read for each application/linkml+yaml resource URI obtained from (example: linkml://www.onvif.org/ver10/agentic/events).

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the LinkML schema as a YAML string in the text field. The ONVIF Client registers this schema in its validator. If multiple schema resources were listed in , this request is repeated for each URI.

section.title: Tool discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends tools/list to obtain the catalogue of available Skills.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns one Tool entry per supported Skill, each with a compiled inputSchema derived from the LinkML model. The example shows get_status only.

section.title: Skill invocation — get_status
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls get_status with no arguments.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the current state of the agentic engine, the list of active functions, and the engine firmware version.

section.title: Skill invocation — list_functions
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls list_functions with no arguments.

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns all functions it supports, their configured/available state, and the LinkML schema URI that governs the configure_function call for each function.

section.title: Skill invocation — configure_function
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls configure_function specifying the function and a config object whose structure matches the LinkML class identified by configSchema (obtained from list_functions).
Response (Device to Client — asynchronous): If configuration requires asynchronous processing, the same tools/call request may return a task handle instead of the final result.
Response (Device to Client — validation error): If the config object violates a schema constraint, the ONVIF Device returns a structured error identifying the failing field.

section.title: Skill invocation — execute_function
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client starts a configured function.
Response (Device to Client — asynchronous start): The task represents only the start operation. It completes when the function is running; it does not remain active for the lifetime of the detection.

The terminal task result shall include the execution identifier, for example exec_fire_001. Events produced by the running function are made available as metadata events, retrievable via events/poll or delivered via webhook.

section.title: Skill invocation — stop_function
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client stops an active execution.
The device may return a task when stopping the execution requires asynchronous processing. The task completes when the execution is stopped.

section.title: Event delivery — catalogue, poll, and webhook examples
section.para: Event type catalogue (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls events/list to discover the event types exposed by the device.
Poll request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls events/poll with a null cursor on the first call.

Poll response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns any matching events produced since the supplied cursor, together with a fresh cursor and the recommended polling interval. The example below shows a FireDetectionEvent carrying a SOSAObservation payload.
Webhook subscription request (Client to Device): Instead of polling, the ONVIF Client MAY register a callback URL for the same event type, when the device advertises "webhook" in delivery.

Webhook delivery (Device to callback endpoint): As matching events occur, the ONVIF Device POSTs each EventOccurrence to the registered callback URL, signed per Standard Webhooks and identifying the subscription.

section.title: Dynamic schema re-registration
section.para: This example shows the procedure triggered when the ONVIF Client receives an EventOccurrence whose @context URI (linkml://onvif/agentic/events/v2) is not yet registered in its schema bundle. The client suspends validation, fetches the schema, and registers it before resuming.

para.emphasis: Poll response with unknown context (Device to Client):

section.para: Schema fetch request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls resources/read with the unknown @context URI.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the new schema. After registration the client validates the suspended event and resumes normal processing.
